Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SECTION 1 GENERAL 
1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies general requirements 
and construction for impregnated paper insulat- 
ed, lead sheathed cables with copper or alumi- 
nium conductors having rated voltages from 
0-65/1-1 kV to 19/33 kV. 

1.2 Maximum Permissible Operating Tempera- 
ture 

The temperatures given in the table below arc 
applicable to draining impregnation and non- 
draining impregnation and are intended as a 
guid*', based on values widely used, for carrying 
out the tests:

•For non-draining type cables only. The temperature 
for draining cables is under consideration. 



1.3 The lead alloy sheathed wire armoured 
copper conductor cable of MIND type covered 
by this standard may also be used in mines, 
provided the combined conductance of the 
armour and lead alloy sheath, or in case when 
the purchaser so desires, the armour alone, 
shall be not less than 50 percent of the largest 
copper condwctor contained in the cable, with 
a minimum of copper equivalent of 15 mm*. To 
satisfy this, substitution of galvanized steel 
wire in armouring by required number of tinned 
copper wires is permissible. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are 
necessaiy adjuncts to this standard, 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the 
following definitions in addition to those given 
in IS 1885 ( Part 32 ): 1971 shall apply. 

3.1 Earthed System 

An electric system which fulfils any o{ the 
following conditions; 

a) The neutral point or the mid-point 
connection is earthed in such a manner 
that, even under fault conditions, the 
maximum voltage that can occur between 
any conductor and the earth does not 
exceed 80 percent of the nominal system 
voltage; 

b) The neutral-point or the mid-point 
connection is not earthed but a protective 
device is installed which automatically 
cuts out any part of the system which 
accidentally becomes earthed; and 

c) In case of ac system only, the neutral 
point is earthed through and arc suppres- 
sion coil with arrangements for isolation 
within one hour of occurrence of the fault 
for the non-radial field cables and within 
8 hours for radial field cables, provided 
that the total of such periods in a year 
does not exceed 125 hours. 



IS 692 : 1994 



3.2 Unearthed System 

An electric system which does not fulfil the 
requirements of the earthed system. 

3.3 Dimensional Values ( Thickness, Cross- 
Section, etc ) 

a) Nominal Values — \ nominal value is a 
value specified always in connection 
with a specified tolerance which has to be 
guaranteed by the manufacturer. 

b) Approximate Values — A value which is 
neither guaranteed nor checked, and is 
used, for example, for the calculation of 
other dimensional values. 

c) Measured Values or Observed Values — 
Values resulting from measurements or 
tests, carried out according to specified 
methods. 

3.4 Type Tests 

Tests required to be made before supply on a 
general commercial basis of a type of cable in 
order to demonstrate satisfactory performance 
characteristics to meet intended application. 

NOTE — These Cests arc of such a nature that after 
they have been made, they need not be repeated 
unless changes are made in the cable materials or 
design which might change performance characteris- 
tics. 



3.5 Acceptance Tests 

Tests carried out on samples taken from a lot 
for the purpose cf acceptance of the lot. 

3.6 Routine Tests 

Tebis made by the manufacturer on all finished 
cable lengths to demonstrate the integrity of 
the cable. 

3.7 Optional Tests 

Special tests to Le carried out, when required, 
by agreement between the purchaser and the 
supplier. 

SECTION |2 IMA TERIALS 

4 CONDUCTOR 

Ihe conductor shall be composed of plain 
copper or aluminium wires complying with 
IS 8130: 1984. 

5 INSULATING PAPER 

5.1 Paper used for cable insulation shall be 
uniform in texture and long fibred and shall not 
contain mechanical wood pulp or esparto. The 
chemicals used in pulping, bleaching or any 
other process of manufacture shall be removed. 
The paper shall be free from dark spots, im- 
perfectly pulped materials, woody matter, lime 
spots, metallic panicles and other deleterious 



substances. It shall also be free from loading 
materials and from gelatine, albumen and resin 
size. 

5.2 The paper shall have chemical characteris- 
tics as given in Annex B. 

5.3 Thickness 

The nominal thickness of individual paper tapes 
shall not exceed 0-15 mm for core insulation and 
0*2 mm for belt insulation. 

6 SCREENING MATERIALS 

6.1 Carbon Paper 

Semi-conducting carbon paper shall be similar 
to the insulating paper in composition and 
blended with finely dispersed carbon during its 
manufactiire. 

6.1.1 The nominal thickness shall be not less 
than 1 mm. 

6.2 Metallic Tape 

It shall be a non-ferrous metal tape made of 
either plain annealed copper or aluminium. The 
nominal thickness shall be not less than 
0-06 mm. 

6.3 Metallized Paper 

It shall comprise aluminium foil bonded to insu- 
lating paper. It shall be perforated to enable 
mass impregnation of the cable. The thickness 
of such aluminium foil shall be not less than 
U-Ol mm. 

7 WORMING MATERIALS 

Worming materials for filling interstitches of 
twin and multicore cables shall comprise paper, 
cotton, jute or any other suitable materials. 
They shall not have any deleterious effect on 
other components of the cables. 

8 COPPER WOVEN FABRIC TAPE 

Copper woven fabric tape for use as binder over 
the laid up cores of screened cables shall com- 
prise cotton tape incorporating interwoven 
copper wires, when applied in cables, it shall 
ensure electrical contact between core screens 
and metallic sheath. 

9 INSULATING COMPOUND 

9.1 The insulating compound for impregnation 
shall be such that the finished cable complies 
with the appropriate requirements of this 
standard. 

9.2 The compound shall be either draining com- 
pound or 'non-draining compound*. 

10 LEAD AND LEAD ALLOYS 

The composition of lead and lead alloys for 
the metallic sheath of the cable shall comply 
with Annex C; 



IS 692 : 1994 



11 ARMOURING MATERIALS 

11.1 Any one of the following armouring 
materials shall be used: 

a) Galvanized steel tape. 

b) Ungalvanized steel tape, 

c) Galvanized round steel wires, 

d) Galvanized steel strip, or 

e) Any non-magnetic material. 

11.2 The armouring material covered by U.l (a) 
to U.l (d) shall comply with IS 3975 : 1988. 

11.3 The specification for non-magnetic armo- 
uring material shall be as agreed between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer. 

12 LAPPED BEDDING AND SERVING 
MATERIALS 

12.1 The materials for lapped bedding aad 
serving shall be as follows: 

a) Textile Materials — Cotton, hessian, jute 
or any other synthetic material; 

b) Plastic Tapes — Tapes of PVC, polyethy- 
lene or any other plastic material; and 

c) Paper ■— It shall be free from pin-holes 
and has minimum thickness of 01 mm. 

12.2 Before application on cable, all natural 
textile materials and paper shall be treated with 
protective compound, 

13 PROTECTIVE COMPOUND 

13.1 All protective compounds used for beddin 
and serving shall be derived from bitumen and 
shall be free from distillation products of coal 
and wood. They shall not have any deleterious 
effect on the lead or lead-alloy sheath, armour 
and bedding and serving materials. They shall 
be of such a nature that in the finished cable 
they do not crack or run at any temperature 
likely 'to be attained in transit to the site or on 
the site, before or after laying or whent he 
cables are m operation. 

13.2 The compound shall adhere properly to 
the armour and the lead or lead-alloy sheath, 
so that if coverings are unwrapped, it shall be 
evident that the metal surfaces were completely 
covered by closely adherent compound before 
removal of the wrapping. 

14 PVC COMPOUND 

PVC compound for extruded bedding or serving 
or both shall comply with the requirement of 
TypeSTl and ST2 of IS 5831:1984 as appli- 
cable.

16 SCREENING 

16.1 Conductor Screening 

All cables having rated voltage above 1 1 kV 
shall have a screen on each conductor consist- 
ing of two layers of semi-conducting carbon 
paper tape. The two layers shall be helically in 
the same direction and breaking joint. 

16.2 Core Screening 

Core screen shall be applied on single core 
cables having rated voltage of 6*35/11 kV and 



IS 692 t 1994 



above, and 3-core aid Score SL cables of 
voltage rating 12-7/22 kV and 19/33 kV. 

16.2.1 For 6-35 kV and 11/11 kV 3-core cables, 
the screen shall be applied on cores if screened 
type cable is required. 

16.2.2 The screen shall be of a layer of non- 
ferrcus metallic tape or perforated metallised 
paper. 

NOTE — Applicaiion of non-ferrous metallic tape 
wiihout gap is not permissible. 

17 CORE INSULATION 

17.1 The conductor in accordance with 15.1 
and 15.2 shall be helically lapped with tapes of 
insulating paper. When applied in the same 
direction, successive layers of paper shall break 
joint so as to form a reasonably smooth cover- 
ing of uniform thickness. 

17.2 Core Identification 

17.2.1 All twin- and multi-core cables shall have 
the identified numbers printed on the outer 
layer of core insulation at frequent intervals. 
The dyes used for printing numbers shall not 
fade beyond recognition, and shall be chemi- 
cally neutral and free from deleterious effect on 
paper. 

17.2.2 Following numbers shall be used for 
core identification: 

a) 0-65/1 -1 kV cable 

1) Twin-core cable i ~ — 

2) Three-core cable 0-12 3 — 

3) Four-core cable 12 3 

b) Three-core cables — 1 2 3 
of l-9/3-3kV and 

higher voltages 

NOTE — The numbers 1 , 2 and 3 indicate the phase 
conductors and 0, rt^e neutral conductor. 

18 LAYING-UP OF CORES 

18.1 Belted Cables 

In twin and multi-core cables, the cores in 
accordance with 16 shall be laid up together 
with interstitches filled with worming material 
and covered with further layers of paper for 
belt insulation to form a reasonably compact 
and circular cable. 

18.2 Screened Cables 

In three-core screened cables, the screened 
cores in accordance with 16 shall be laid up 
together with interstitches filled with worming 
material, and further lapped with a binder of 
copper woven fabric tape. 



18.3 Screened SL Cables 

In screened SL cables, the screened cores mass- 
impregnated in accordance with 19 lead or lead 
alloy sheathed in accordance with 20 and bedded 
in accordance with 21 shall be laid up together 
with interstitches filled with compounded worm- 
ing material and followed by one or more 
layers of textile material. 

18.4 Direction of Laying Up 

For all twin and multi-core cables the direction 
of laying up shall be right-hand. 

19 IMPREGNATION 

19.1 Insulation, paper-screens, fillers and 
binders tape ( if any ) shall be dried and im- 
pregnated with an insulating compound. 

19.2 When specifically agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer, the cables 
impregnated with non-draining compound shall 
comply with the drainage test. 

NOTE — Where the cables are to be installed on 
verticle runs or gradients, the use of non>draining 
compound is recommended. 

19.3 Thickness of Insulation 

The thickness of insulation excluding all screen- 
ing materials shall not be less than the value 
specified in the relevant tables. 

20 LEAD OR LEAD ALLOY SHEATH 

20.1 After impregnation, the cable shall be 
covered with a metallic lead or lead alloy sheath 
as specifically agreed to between the purchaser 
and the manufacturer. 

20.2 The sheath shall be extruded directly on 
the cable in the form of a seamless tube. It shall 
be reasonably close-fitting, impervious to 
moisture and free from pin-holes, joints, mended 
place and other defects. Stop-marks of the press 
are not considered as defects. 

20.3 Thickness 

The thickness of sheath shall not fall below the 
value specified in the relevant tables. 

21 BEDDING 

21.1 Armoured cable shall have a protective 
bedding over lead or lead alloy sheath. 

21.2 Lapped Bedding 

21.2.1 Except in SL cables, the bedding applied 
shall consist of suitably impregnated and com- 
pounded papers era combination of two layers 
of impregnated and compounded paper followed 
by one or more layers of compounded fibrous 
material. 



IS 692 : 1994 



21.2.1.1 As an alternative to paper tapes, it 
shall be permissible to use plastic tapes. 

21.2.1.2 The impregnation of bedding of natural 
textile material may be made with bituminous 
compound of other preservative material. 

21.2.2 In SL cables, the bedding shall consist 
of bedding over each lead sheath followed by a 
covering layer over the laid up lead sheathed 
and lapped cores. The bedding over each lead 
sheath shall consist of one of the following: 

a) At least two layers of impregnated and 
compounded paper, 

b) 2-Iayers of plastic tape, or 

c) l-layer of impregnated paper and layer of 
impregnated textile material, both being 

compounded. 

21.2.2.1 The covering over the laid up cores 
shall consist of one or more layers of impregnat- 
ed and compounded natural textile material. 

21.2.2.2 The impregnation of bedding of natural 
textile material may be made with bituminous 
compound or other preservative material. 

21.2.3 Thickness of Bedding 

The total thickness of the protection between 
lead sheath and armour measured after appli- 
cation of the armouring should have the 
approximate value of 1-5 mm. 

21.3 Extruded Bedding 

21.3.1 When an extruded PVC bedding is applied 
over a lead sheath, it shall be preferably black 
and of type ST2 of IS 5831 : 1984, 

21.3.2 Thickness 

The thickness of extruded bedding shall not 
fall below the value specified in the relevant 
tables, 

22 AKMOUR 

22.1 Type of Armour 

For cables having calculated diameter over lead 
or lead-alloy sheath up to and including 13 mm, 
the armour shall consist of galvanized round 
steel wires only. Where calculated diameter 
over lead or lead alloy sheath is more than 
13 mm y the armour shall consist of galvanized 
round steel wires or galvanized steel strips or 
two layers of galvanized or ungalvanized steel 
tape. 

22.1.1 In case of SL cables, the basis of selec- 
tion of the type of armour shall apply to the 
calculated diameter over laid up cores. 

22.1.2 Where armouring is required for single- 
core cables intended for use in ac system, it 



shall consist of non-magnetic material and shall 
be as specifically agreed to between the purchaser 
and the manufacturer. In case of single-core 
cables intended for use in dc system, armouring 
shall be done by galvanized steel wire strip. 

22.2 Application 

22.2.1 Double Steel Tape Armour 

22.2.1.1 When steel tapes are ungalvanized, they 
shall be thoroughly coated on both sides with 
protective compound before being applied to 
the cable. 

22.2.1.2 The two layers of tape shall be laid 
helically with a left-hand lay so that outer tape 
is approximately central over the gaps of inner 
tape. 1 he gap between the adjacent turns of 
each tape shall not exceed 50 percent of the 
tape width. The outer tape shall overlap the 
inner tape on both sides by not less than 15 per- 
cent of ihc tape width. 

22.2.1.3 The nominal thickness of uncompound- 
ed steel tape shall be as specified in the relevant 
tables. 

22.2.2 Single Wire or Strip Armour 

The ai-mour shall consist of a single layer of 
galvanized sieel wire or strip and shall be applied 
with left-hand lay. The nominal diameter of 
wire or dimensions of strip shall be as specified 
in the relevant table. 

22.2.3 Double Wire or Strip Armour 

22.2.3.1 The armour shall consist of two layers 
of galvanized steel wires or strips. The inner 
layer of wires or strips shall be applied wiih 
left-hand lay. The ouier layer shall be applied 
with right-hand lay except in special cases when 
specifically agreed to between the purchaser and 
'the manufacturer. 

22.2.3.2 Separator 

A separator consisting of a layer of compounded 
textile material shall be applied between the 
two layers of armour wires or strips. 

22.2.3.3 Foi both layers, the nominal diameter 
of wires Or dimensions of strips shall be the 
same as for single wire or strip armoured 
cable. 

22.3 Binder Tape 

A binder tape may be applied over flat steel 
wire armour, or if necessary, over round steel 
wire armour. It may be applied in the same 
direction as the armour or in the opposite 
direction. 

22.3.1 It shall consist of galvanized steel tape 
having a nominal thickness of not less than 
0*2 mm. The minimum thickness shall not 



IS 692 t 1994 



fait below the specified nominal value by more 
than 10 percent. 

22.4 Joints 

The joints in the armour/strips or tapes shall 
be made by brazing or welding and the surface 
irregularities shall be removed. A joint in any 
wire/strip or tape shall be at least 300 mm from 
the nearest joint in any other armour wire/strip 
or tape in the completed cable. 

23 SERVING AND OVERALL SHEATH 

23.1 Textile Serving on Armour 

The serving having an approximate thiclcness 
of 2 mm shall consist of a suitable number of 
compounded layers of textile material. In order 
to prevent adhesion, a coating of white wash or 
suitable material shall be applied to the outside 
of the cable. 

NOTE — The impregnation of textile serving may be 
made with either bituminous compounds or other 
preservative materials. 

23.2 Extruded Outer Sheath for Unarmoured or 
Armoured Cables 

This shall be black preferably and of type ST2 
of IS 5831 : 1984. 

23.2.1 Thickness 

Where the sheath is applied over the lead sheath 
of an unarmoured cable, the average thickness 
determined by taking a number of measurements 
shall not be less than the value specified in the 
relevant tables and the smallest of the measur- 
ed values shall not fall below the specified 
value 4- 0-2 mm. For this purpose, the calculat- 
ed minimum permissible value shall be rounded 
off to an accuracy of 001 mm. 

23.2.1.1 When the shealh is applied over 
armoured cables, the thickness shall not fall 
below the value specified in the relevant tables. 

23.3 The thickness of extruded PVC serving 
shall not fall below the value specified in the 
relevant table. 

NOTE — For embossed cables, the point at which 
the mcnsurements made shall not coincide with any 
cmbo&sing.

24.2 AcceptiiBce Tests 

The following shall constitute acceptance tests: 

a) Conductor resistance test, 

b) Test for thickness of insulation, 

c) Test for thickness of lead and lead alloy 
sheath, 

d) Test for thickness of steel tape or dia- 
meter of round wires or dimensions of 
steel strips, 

e) Dielectric power factor/voltage test 
( for 19/33 kV cables only ), 

f ) Voltage test, and 

g) Test for thickness of extruded PVC bed- 
ding and serving. 

24.2.1 A recommended sampling plan for 
acceptance tests is given in Annex D. 

24.3 Routine Tests 

The following shall constitute routine tests: 

a) Conductor resistance test, 

b) Dielectric power factor/voltage test 
( for 19/33 kV cables only ), and 

c) Voltage test. 

24.4 Optional Tests 

The following shall constitute optional tests:

24.6 Breaking Strength and Elongation Test for 
Insulation 

This test shall be in accordance with IS 10810 
( Part 8 ) : 1964 and when tested thus the 
breaking strength of the test strip shall not fall 
below 700 N mm of thickness and the elonga- 
tion at break shall not be less than 1-5 percent. 

24.7 Impulse Test 

24.7.1 An impulse test as laid down in 24.7.2 
may be applied as a type test for 12-7/22 kV 
cables and 19/33 kV cables. For 6-35/11 kV 
cables, this test is not required. It shall be 
considered sufficient if the impulse level of 
75 kV is certified by the manufacturer. 

24.7.2 For orders for cables of length of 5 km 
and above, a sample of 10 m length taken from 
every 6 km of the cable shall be subjected to 
impulse voltage test which shall be carried out 
at room temperature in accordance with 
IS 10810 ( Part 47 ) : 1984 and no break-down 
of the insulation shall occur. The impulse test

24 5 Test for Thickness of Insulation 

24.5.1 The measurement of the thickness of the 
insulation shall be made on a representative 
sample of the cable not more than 150 mm in 
length, taken not less than 300 mm from the 
end of a factory length. 

24.5.2 Procedure 

The thickness of insulation shall be determined 
by bunching together the individual paper tapes 
removed from the finished cable (without 
removing the surplus compound from the 
papers ) and measuring the total thickness with 
dead weight dial type micrometer having the

top clamp shall be at least 50 mm.

24.13 Bending Test for Finished Cables 

This test shall be carried out in accordance 
with IS 10810 ( Part 50 ) : 1984 and shall meet 
the following requirements: 

a) The cable sample withstands the applied 
voltage test without failure; and 

b) The visual examination shows that the 
serving is free from splits; the armour is 
not noticeable disposed and the sheath 
is free from splits or cracks.

SECTION 5 IDENTIFICATION, PACKING 
AND MARKING 

25 END MARKING 

The ends of factory lengths of cables shall be 
capped and sealed with plumbing metal, the 
cores being suitably insulated from the cap. 
The caps shall be marked with letters *A* 
and •Z', *A' being the end at which the sequence 
of the core numbers ( see 16.2 ) is clockwise 
and 'Z* the end at which the sequence is anti- 
clockwise. 

26 VOLTAGE IDENTIFICATION 

26.1 All 3-3 kV cables and above with lapped 
serving shall be identified by means of galvanis- 
ed steel wire of diameter 1-4 mm or alternatively 
a galvanised steel strip of size 0*4 x 0*8 mm 
applied longitudinally as follows: 

a) Unarmoured cables : Over the outer 

layer of paper in 
bedding 

b) Armoured cables : Over the armour- 

ing. 

26.2 Where the cable is provided with extruded 
PVC serving this shall be embossed legibly with 
the words 'HIGH VOLTAGE*. 

27 MANUFACTURER'S IDENTIFICATION 

The manufacturer's name or trade mark shall 
be identified throughout the length of the cable 
by a tape under the sheath, bearing the manu- 
facturer's name or trade mark and the year of 
manufacture. As an alternative, for cables with 
an outer shealh of PVC, the identification of 
the manufacturer and the year of manufacture 
may be by priming, indentation or embossing on 
the outersheath. 

28 CABLE IDENTIFICATION CODE 

The following code is recommended for distin- 
guishing' the type of cable required: 



Single round steel wire armour W 

Single steel strip armour F 

Double round steel wire armour WW 

Double steel strip armour FF

ANNEX D 
( Clause 24.2.1 ) 

SAMPLING OF CABLES 



D-1 LOT 

D-Ll In any consignment, the cables of the same 

size manufactured under essentially similar 

conditions of production shall be grouped 

together to constitute a lot. 

D.2 SCALE OE SAMPLING 

D-2.1 Samples shall be taken and tested from 

each lot for ascertaining the conformity of the 

lot to the requirements of the specification. 

D-2.2 The number of samples to be selected 

shall depend on col 1 and 2 as indicated below. 

The samples shall be taken at random.

D-2.2. 1 In order to ensure the randomness of 
selection, random number tables shall be used 
( IS 4905 : 1968 ). 

D-3 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERION 
FOR CONFORMITY 

D-3.1 Suitable lengths of test samples shall be 
taken from each of the drum selected. These 
test samples shall be subjected to each of the 
acceptance tests ( 24.2 ). A test sample is called 
defective if it fails in any one of the acceptance 
tests. If the number of defective is less than or 
equal to the corresponding permissible number 
given in col 3, under D-2.2 the lot shall be 
declared as conforming to the requirements of 
acceptance tests; otherwise not.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Power Cables Sectional Committee had been approved by the Elcctrotechnical Division 
Council. 

This standard was originally published in 1957 and subsequently revised in 1965 and 1973. This third 
revision has been brought out lo take into account the experience gained during this period in the 
manufacture of these types of cables m the country and to bring this standard in line with international 
practice to the extent considered appropriate. 

The correct type of cables should be selected for the system keeping in view whether the system is 
earthed or unearthed. 

It should be realised that in an electric system where an earth fault is not automatically and promptly 
eliminated, the extra stresses on the insulation of the cable during the earth fault reduce the life of 
cable to a certain extent. Therefore, if the system is expected to be operated quite often with a prolon- 
ged earth fault, it is necessary to select the cables suitable for unearthed system. 

In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from lEC Publications 55-1 ( 1978 ) and 
55-2(1981) 'Paper-insulated melal-shealhcd cables for rated voltages up to 18/30 kV : Part I Tests 
and Part 2 General and constructional requirements', issued by the International Elcctrotechnical 
Commission ( lEC ). 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)*. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded oil' value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of stardardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of *BIS Handbook' and ^Standards: Monthly Additions'. 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc: No. ETD 9 ( 2965 )
